en: H-Hey, what happened...?! Old\nman! Everyone!
Damn it... To be found by a\nRaza ship... I thought the bribes\nwould have cleared things up...
I have finally found you, Mr.\nHeath Bureau.
...What... did you say?
I never imagined you would be\nabsorbed by the pirates of the\nStardust Bazaar.

While I am grateful they take in
refugees, it is problematic that
they force even children to do
illegal work.
...Who on earth are you...?

I am Lieutenant Jeanne
Marswest of the Raza Space
Force. Your parents have filed
a missing person's report for
you.
...He... Heath!
Mmph... Ah, sorry, I drifted off\nfor a second.
...You were having a nightmare.
Just a dream from a long time\nago. What, were you worried\nabout me?
...Your sleep-talking was\nirritating.
My bad. So, if you woke me up,\ndoes that mean we've arrived?
...Yes. We promised to do the\njob.
Yeah, yeah. Hmm... so, who's\ngetting off?
Euwin, Welch, and Karlyn.
Who's the contact and where is\nit?
Ober's smuggler. On the <font color=yellow>moon\nRigas</font> of Planet Incal.
Roger that. Well then, let's get\nto work!
...Heath, I'm telling you this just\nin case...

I know. Up until four years ago,
I was a family man too. My
weapon is the same as it was
back then.
...Then, fine.
Well then, I'm off.
This place is so desolate. It\nfeels like it was practically\nmade for black market deals!

Looking down from the sky, I
saw city ruins in the distance.
It looked so prosperous; I
wonder why no one is there.
Well, there are reasons for it.\nSorry about that. The rules for\nthese deals are a pain.
It's okay. I'm used to it, and it\nhappens all the time.
All the time? We've been\nwalking all over the place for\nno reason!

Besides, being this exposed,
isn't there a risk of someone
sniping us from those ruins and
just stealing our goods?

It's a common black market
tactic. They stay alert for
authorities or ambushes, and
sometimes, they'll even strike
from a distance.
Huh!? "Strike"? You mean they\nactually attack us? Why would\nanyone do that!

They hold back a little, but it's
a way of deciding that they
won't do business with any
fools who make mistakes here.

Sigh. It feels strange knowing
that Eu's experiences traveling
Rubarika are actually helping
him survive in space.
Maybe it just means that\nhumans never change.
Well, looks like our chatting\ntime is up.
Just in time.
I hope it's not Thornite.
Don't worry. It looks like...
It's definitely our business\npartner!!

They won't launch a surprise
attack, but they should be
quite formidable. Stay on your
guard!
Smuggler: Heh... looks like the\nRose family still has some\nimpeccable skill left in them.
...Not really.
Smuggler: Don't be so modest.

Smuggler: I feared Gartoga was
on the decline since the cargo
was small, but I was completely
wrong.

Smuggler: I haven't seen Gems
of this high purity in years.
How on earth did you get your
hands on these?
...It's a trade secret.
Smuggler: I figured. I'd like to\nkeep a good relationship with\nyou all moving forward.

Fighting the creatures and
machines released by clients
at every relay point, and only
beginning trade upon victory...

...Why use such an inefficient
method? It feels as though
both parties are merely
incurring losses...

That's just how wartime
smuggling goes. You never
know where the military's nets
are. It was common back in
Rubarika, too.

We can't defy Lavarnia now.
Unless we see an incredibly
atrocious outcome, we have no
choice but to comply.
...Coro, how is it?
...So far, I haven't found any\ntraces that look like Eve.
...I see.
Tika. Pull yourself together. For\nnow, we have no choice but to\ntake things one step at a time.
Yeah... You're right.
Alright, I'm back safe and\nsound!
Welcome back, Euwin! Good\njob, everyone. How did it go?
...The smugglers here didn't\nknow anything about the\nThornite either.
And of course, regarding Eve...

No. They said they had no idea
about those black monsters,
like the ones Givel was
summoning.
...I see.
I'm not sure if it's a substitute,\nbut I did hear something\ninteresting.

Apparently, over the last five
months or so, Ober has been
pushing back the Raza army in
various places.

She was saying it's been a
rapid advance since the start
of the war, sounding all
pleased about it. Honestly.

What's the reality, then? If the
tide of war shifted that
drastically, you'd feel it on the
front lines.

The front Isabel was on was
basically just trying to stop
them from attacking a civilian
spaceport.

We weren't in a position to
oversee the entire war, and I
haven't heard any rumors of
some place losing like an idiot.
Well, there's always the\npossibility that information is\nbeing controlled.

Could it be that the very
reports of Ober winning are
themselves a result of
information control?

Perhaps Ober is spreading
such rumors to boost the
morale of the military and the
people...
No. I think Ober is actually\nwinning.
...I think so, too.
Why can you say that with\nsuch certainty?
No matter how much you\ncontrol information, the prices\nof goods and money don't lie.

Even if they're smugglers,
they're still merchants. They're
probably doing really well for
themselves.
...I agree. ...Wait, Welch, were\nyou a merchant as well?
I was a blacksmith. The price\nof metal is directly affected by\nwar, after all.
Prices went up and down so\nmuch it was almost\nentertaining.
It's possible they're\nmanipulating information even\nafter controlling the markets.
Even so, that would mean the\neconomy has enough leeway to\nabsorb those losses.
If even the lowliest merchants\nare feeling a boom, something\nreal must be happening.
Hmm... I'm a bit out of my\ndepth with such talk...
Even big sister Verda has\nthings she's not good at.

I'm quite bad at many things.
To do business, one must be
able to read the hearts of the
people, I suppose.
And when it comes to that... I\ncouldn't even read the heart of\na single comrade...
...Yeah. You're right... I wonder\nwhat happened to big sister\nEve...
...Judging by the situation, it\nmeans your companion... Eve\nstole our Gems.
T-That's...

...These are precious goods our
family spent so much time and
money to collect. Lending you
a ship is out of the question at
this rate.
H-How much money are we\ntalking about?
If you intend to compensate us\nwith money, you are being\nshallow.

Even with money, we couldn't
prepare the goods for our
customers. The loss of trust
we'd suffer is worth far more
than any amount of money...
Y-You're right...

In practical terms, even if we
caught Evelysse now, the lost
Gems wouldn't just return to
us.
His summons require a price to\nbe paid.
...Does that mean she's already\nused them?
It's natural to assume so.
Ugh... W-Well, what are we\nsupposed to do then...?
...Lover. Right now, I'm just\nstanding here all alone in the\nBazaar.

I'll earn back every single Gem
lost when I went from being a
lowlife to returning to the Rose
family. So, please, Captain...
Heath! That's...!

Even with how little time I've
known her, I know Eve isn't the
kind of woman who would
commit such a lawless act.

But since this is the reality, it's
my responsibility for relying on
you all and introducing her to
the Lovers.
...How much do you think your\nown worth is?

Even if you worked for the rest
of your life, you wouldn't earn
even half of the Gems that
were just lost.
...W-what is it, Captain?
Responsibility... Captain, don't\ntell me...
...Do you possess high-purity\nGems?

You didn't even know what
Gems meant in the Azurite
system, so how can you claim
to have high purity?
...Fine. But you must have seen\nthe number of Gems that were\nhere.
If the quality isn't enough to\nmake up for the quantity, I\nwon't accept them.
If that happens, I'll have no\nchoice but to ask Papa for a\nfinal decision.
I will not compromise. Be\nprepared.

Even though the amount wasn't
nearly enough, Lavarnia-san
went silent the moment she
saw them.
Ricardo said he would not ask\nfor details to avoid\nunnecessary interference, but...

Since it has come to this, it
would be wise for you to at
least know how Gems are
utilized in the Azurite system.

You're right. If people are
fighting wars to steal them and
smuggling is rampant, they
must be incredibly important...
W-What was that!?

Energy signatures from
firearms. A spacecraft is
engaging in combat at
extremely close range!
What!?
Don't tell me one of the armies\nfound us?
No, there shouldn't be any\nRaza or Ober ships in this\narea.
I'm confirming it with the data\nbeing sent from Rekoro.
Valka, could this be the\ntransport vessel from our\nearlier business partner?

It appears so. The smuggler's
vessel just fired live
ammunition in the upper
atmosphere of this satellite,
Rigas.
It was only one shot, so maybe\nthey just destroyed some large\ndebris...
...Wait, what!?
S-Signal lost! I've confirmed a\nheat signature from the\ntransport vessel's explosion!
What does this mean? Was it\nshot down by a long-range\nattack!?

N-No, that shouldn't be
possible... Besides, there's no
sign of such a reaction
anywhere...!
Hmm!?
What is it this time!

No, I can't be certain because
we weren't able to replace the
Overman's optical sensors,
but...

I spotted a small combat craft
that appears to have attacked
the smuggler's transport
vessel. I'll put it on the screen.
...Is that a combat craft? It's\nblending in with the color of\nspace, so it's hard to tell.
If the enemy went down, is\nthere any sign that this\ncombat craft fired anything?
That's the thing... I couldn't\ndetect anything.

I checked the data from AI
Rekoro; there are only traces
of shots fired from the
transport vessel's side.
As for the transport vessel in\nquestion...
Ugh... this is...
The hull is completely\nfractured...

There's no way anyone could
have survived. It looks like it
just hit a meteorite or
something.
Can you not tell which faction\nthat supposed combat craft\nbelongs to?

First of all, I can't be certain if
it's even a combat craft... but
its shape looks similar to an
Ober vessel.

However, at least when
cross-referencing with the
Overman's data, no matching
ships were found.
...In Ober, many different races\ndispatch volunteers and\nmercenaries to the military.

I can't track every ship, and
the Overman only contains
data regarding my personal
interests.
You shouldn't rely on it too\nheavily.
By the way, I have one more\nunpleasant report.
What could there possibly be?
Regarding that mysterious\ncombat craft... it flew off in the\ndirection we are heading.
What's more, it moved as if it\nwere tracing the ideal course I\ncalculated.
It couldn't just be a\ncoincidence...
You'd be wise not to assume\nthat.
...I thought so.
There's no use dwelling on it.

Heath, Lavarnia. Let's head
toward that ship to attempt a
rescue first, then we'll move on
to the next point.
And also... there's something I\nwant you to tell me.
...About what?
The war between Raza and\nOber. As much detail as you\ncan.
...Originally, Ober and Raza\nachieved space expansion at\nalmost the same time.
There are a total of 36 planets\nin the Azurite system.
The planets in the habitable\nzone are Planet Raza and\nPlanet Ober.
Next are the moon Rigas and\nthe Stardust Bazaar.
...And finally, <font color=yellow>Planet Lazuli</font>.
Out of these, humans only\ninhabit Raza, Ober, and the\nBazaar.

And that planet Raza and Ober
are fighting over, the one that
old man Gartoga mentioned, is
Planet Lazuli.
<font color=blue>Lavarnia</font> The moon Rigas was\na mining planet.

Gems were abundant across
the planet, so Raza and Ober,
new to space expansion,
shared these resources
peacefully.

<font color=blue>Welch</font> But now they're fighting
over Gems, aren't they? Why
can't they be like they were
back then?
<font color=blue>Heath</font> It was an era shortly\nafter they expanded into\nspace.

Both were far more primitive
than today; forget combat
ships, even leaving their home
planets was a life-or-death
gamble.

At that time, both sides knew
fighting other humans in the
same star system they'd just
met was not a wise move.
<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> It's ironic that they were\nonly peaceful because they\nlacked the means to fight.

<font color=blue>Heath</font> It wasn't just a matter
of means; at that time, Raza
was facing a planet-wide
depletion of energy resources.
It seems they were on the\nbrink of planetary extinction if\nthey couldn't secure Gems.

In such a situation, if there was
a chance to acquire resources
peacefully, anyone who wasn't
a complete fool would take it.

<font color=blue>Verda</font> It is quite a feat they
developed enough to expand
into space despite such
destitution.

<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> But if Raza gains
momentum... won't Ober be
forced to step in instead of
just watching?

<font color=blue>Lavarnia</font> As for Ober, they
were in an era plagued by
conflict between different
races.

Civil wars raged across the
planet; the space colonization
project's success would decide
if a unified planetary
government could be
established.

They simply didn't have the
luxury of fighting the people
they had just made first
contact with.

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> I see. Even in Rubarika,
we certainly didn't have the
luxury of making other enemies
during the Holy Land War.

<font color=blue>Heath</font> Yeah... anyway, at that
time, both planets were still
holding hands and getting
along reasonably well.
<font color=blue>Heath</font> Besides, the Gems\nmined on the satellite Rigas...

...were far more efficient than
the energy Raza used for
space development, allowing
both planets to achieve a
massive technological leap.

<font color=blue>Tika</font> So, you're saying they
started fighting because their
technology improved enough to
wage war?

<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> No, that's not the
fundamental cause. You can
tell just by looking at the
current situation on Rigas.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Is it because the Gem\nreserves on Rigas have run\ndry?
<font color=blue>Heath</font> Exactly. All that's left on\nRigas now are old-fashioned\nfossil fuels like coal and oil.
A modern society accustomed\nto Gems couldn't possibly use\nsuch inefficient energy.
As the Gems ran out, the\npeople began to leave this\nplanet like a receding tide.
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> So, that's why Raza and\nOber began fighting to find\nnew Gem mining sites.
<font color=blue>Lavarnia</font> ...It seems things\ndidn't turn that hostile quite so\nsuddenly back then, though...

Relations soured about 100
years ago, after a new,
massive Gem vein was
discovered to replace Rigas.
It's a place you guys know, too.
...No way.
The Stardust Bazaar!?
...Yes. An asteroid cluster\ncrossing the habitable zone of\nthe Azurite system.
Someone once pioneered that\narea.

He was a man who established
Gem research in Rigas back
when Gems first started
gaining attention,

and he was beloved by the
people of both Raza and Ober.
He's the founder of the
Stardust Bazaar.

Hmm...? So a figure from the
earliest days of Gem research
was still alive until just 100
years ago?

Gem research has been
ongoing for centuries, hasn't
it? Is it even possible for such
a long-lived individual to exist?

Some species of Ober live a
long time. However, it's not
known for certain whether he
was Raza or Ober.

...He was from Raza, I believe.
But records say that no matter
how you looked at him, he
didn't look Human.
His name is only passed down\nas "<font color=yellow>Kevin</font>".

And so... the researchers from
Rigas led by Kevin made the
conflict between Raza and
Ober irreversible.
...I see. So the people of Rigas\njust went ahead and made the\nStardust Bazaar independent.
I see. This moon is the same\nsize as a normal rocky planet.

If the local population and Gem
mining tech moved here as
one, independence might be
possible.
But why would they do that so\nsuddenly?
It's obvious that doing so would\ncause trouble for both the\nRaza and the Ober.

Normally, wouldn't the Raza
and Ober team up to stop the
independence and become
enemies with the Bazaar?
Monopoly.
Huh?
If that story is true, then the\nGems are under the Bazaar's\nmonopoly.
They've got a stranglehold on\nthe energy supply. There's no\nway they could fight back.
It means no idiot is going to\npick a fight and say, "Give us\nyour fuel."
...I see.
I don't understand why Kevin\nforced his independence.

As a result, a three-way
deadlock was established
between Raza, Ober, and the
Bazaar...
...But.

That's when, twenty years ago,
the issue of sovereignty over
Planet Lazuli suddenly dropped
out of the blue.

The planet Lazuli is a world of
sand and wasteland. It has no
underground resources, no
plant life, and no water.
While the atmosphere was the\ntype that could support the\nRaza and most Ober,

It was judged unsuitable for
habitation and ignored since
the early days of space
exploration.
What? There's an atmosphere\nthe Raza can breathe, but no\nwater?

Yeah, that's right. I passed by
there once on a mission, and
it's a lonely, reddish-brown
rock.
...I see. That is strange.
The Bazaar didn't pay any\nattention to Lazuli either.

It's too far away to serve as a
relay point for starships, and
there are no useful planets or
resources nearby.

So, in truth... the Bazaar
doesn't actually understand
why the Raza and the Ober are
fighting over Lazuli.
Huh? Are you serious?

Dead serious. To be honest,
even as a former member of
the Raza military, I was never
given a clear reason.

Within the Raza military, the
official story is that we're
securing a bridgehead for
space exploration and
searching for new Gems veins,
but...

Even the Ober refugees who
came to the Bazaar didn't
seem to understand why they
needed planet Lazuli.

Hey, hey... You're telling me
they've been fighting for nearly
20 years without even knowing
what they're fighting for?
Yeah. And the\ncost-performance is absolute\ngarbage.

Honestly, I think it would be
much more economical to just
bow our heads to the Bazaar
and buy Gems.

There are actually opinions like
that, and even in Raza, a sense
of war-weariness is starting to
set in.

Regardless of the reason, after
20 years, you can't just stop
just because the original
problem was solved.
Both sides have been killing\neach other for far too long.
...Well, that's how it is.
Hmm, I still don't understand\nwhat Raza and Ober are\nultimately seeking from Lazuli,

I finally understand why the
Bazaar remains neutral despite
such fierce conflict between
the two.
I also get why Lavarnia's father\ncalled it a trivial planet.

But even if it is a planet like
that, there must be a reason
why Raza and Ober have been
fighting over it for 20 years.
*Sigh*... I just hope we don't\nend up having to go to Planet\nLazuli at some point...

Captain, we have arrived at
the coordinates where the
smuggler's ship sank.	machine	gemma-4-26B-A4B-it/UD-Q4_K_M/v2+story-v1/llama.cpp-b11443/t0	2026-10-06		
6022_070_27	6950007d7622f8ea2100a42159d10f16fb3521c0	...Regrettably, there appear to
be no survivors. I need
everyone to come to the
Bridge.
Understood. Wrap it up, let's\nmove.
...Karlyn.
What?
How many more years do you\nthink you'll live?
Huh? Where is this coming\nfrom all of a sudden?
The Holy Land War finally\nended, and yet, once again, in\nthe future...

I just thought that if this
happened in the Daftine where
Tika and the others are born,
I'd hate it.
...Two hundred years from now,\nhuh? That's actually quite\npossible, which is a problem.
Don't say "a problem."
But, I'll leave everything in your\nhands for when you finally\nreach the end of your lifespan.

Until then, you'd better do your
best. Though, it doesn't look
like you'd die even if I killed
you.
Just what do you think I am...?
This... Just what kind of force\ncould cause this much\ndamage?
It's been completely snapped in\ntwo.

I scanned the fracture. It
wasn't caused by heat, but by
the impact of colliding with a
massive object.
So you're saying it was an\naccident?
That possibility cannot be ruled\nout. However, there is one\nstrange thing.

A specific substance was
floating only around the
wreckage, containing
components not found in the
surrounding rocks or debris.
I am running an analysis on it\nnow.

Administrator Koro is pushing
the Overman's analysis to its
limit to investigate the
substance.

It will take some time as I must
communicate the data with AI
Rekoro, but I expect it to be
completed in about half a day.

No, we'll leave the wreckage. If
it were a proper ship, the black
box would continue to emit a
signal for a while.
All we can do is pray that\nOber's lot picks it up.

...It can't be helped. The
Overman was a pirate ship, and
their opponents were
smugglers.
We both have to be prepared\nto become space debris if an\naccident occurs.
One wrong move, and we could\nhave ended up just like them...

...It may sound heartless, but
we are recovering those Gems.
If they can't take them back,
we can still make use of them.

Actually, that's the problem.
I've been scanning the area,
but there's no sign of the
container holding the Gems.
...What?
The impact of the sinking might\nhave sent it flying far away.

Unless the container is
equipped with a transmitter,
searching for it will be
impossible.
...What a waste.
They certainly are resilient,\naren't they?

It can't be helped. We must
head to the next point. To
ensure their sacrifice wasn't in
vain, we will proceed with
caution.
So this is a sample of\nwhatever destroyed that\nsmuggler's ship?
I can't say for certain, though.

It's much more brittle than the
surrounding rock, so unless it
hits at high speed, I doubt a
large mass would cause much
impact.
Ho... It certainly crumbles quite\neasily.

I suppose I should have had
them modify the hardware of
the Overman a little more after
all...
If you assume it's the same as\nthe GFSS-3214F, you'll run into\nall sorts of delays...

I wonder how much longer this
component analysis will take.
Verda, could you give me a
hand?
Very well. Let me see... It is\nindeed a primitive component\nscanner...
Is this not a silicon-based\nsubstance?
Hmm?
Eh? Silicon?
Look at this part. It looks\nexactly like the silicic acid\nformed inside plants.
Is that something you can tell\nat a glance?
On the Ex Giva, we had to\nperiodically improve the\ngrain-based foods we grew.
Silicon is essential for a plant's\nphotosynthetic capacity and\nstress reduction,

They adjusted it precisely to
match plant changes or the
characteristics of the races
consuming them.

Begin identification starting
from the silicon-based
molecular structure. It is likely
a closely related substance.
Understood. I'll give it a try.
...Even so.
Hmm?

How is it that you can perform
such calm analysis, yet you
turn into that when you're
faced with Eve or Karlyn's
Gems?

It is the difference between
the known and unknown. When
people try to advance by their
own strength, they struggle
pathetically.
I feel like it's not quite at that\nlevel...

If you keep being so rude, you'll
earn "points," and you'll find it
quite frightening when we
return to our ship.

Ah, that system where
mysterious points suddenly
accumulate... how nostalgic! I'll
get back to the analysis!!
There is no use running away...

But even if it were a
silicon-based substance, I
wonder why such a thing would
be floating there.

Is the next point our last? I'm
glad there haven't been any
major troubles since the first
job, but...
To think the handoff is on an\nasteroid near Planet Lazuli at\nthe very end.
Is it really safe to trade so\nclose to such a heavy combat\nzone?

...The handoff point itself is
fine; I had them designate a
location far from the
battlefield.

Besides, our next contact isn't
some shady smuggler like the
others. Because of that, the
reward is extraordinary.
So, I'm being selective about\nwho handles this next\ntransaction.
Is it not okay for it to be me,\nEuwin, Welch, and Karlyn like\nusual?
...You should stay hidden this\ntime. And if possible, Captain\nand Ricardo too.
And what is the reason for\nthat?
Our next contact is the Raza\nSpace Force 5th Fleet.

You and Ricardo-san look like
soldiers at a glance, so it'll be
a bit troublesome if you're
spotted.
The 5th Fleet!? We're dealing\ndirectly with the military!?\nWon't we get intercepted?!
...That won't happen. We've\nbeen doing business with the\n5th Fleet for nearly ten years.
No, but... what if something like\nthat happens again...?
...I'm surprised you can even\nsay that out loud.
Ah, no.
...I've already looked into that\nwoman's affiliation.
The 1st Fleet. She was a\npolitical officer for the frontline\nunits.
I suppose you could call it my\nfather's mistake...
Since then, both Raza and\nOber have only dealt with\npeople they can truly trust.
It's made our finances difficult,\nbut it's a price worth paying\nfor safety.
I-I see.

So, if you do end up returning
to her command, please don't
report the 5th Fleet's illicit
dealings.
The money coming from the\n5th Fleet is what keeps the\nrefugees in the Bazaar alive.
It may be illegal, but it is an\nunchangeable fact. Do not\nforget that.
...I know. The Boss's integrity\nisn't the kind that follows those\nrules.
I wonder about that.
So, are you sure you want to\nleave Heath out and just have\nthe three of us?

...Truthfully, it would be
reassuring if you came, Karlyn,
but... we need to deliver the
cargo to that ship.
Foxtail's Karlyn likely won't be\nallowed in.
That's why I'm asking you,\nEuwin, Welch, and Tika.
Understood. Is there anything I\nshould be careful about?

...As long as you don't go
anywhere other than the
